use_case_name: Add Files to an Existing Archive

claims.content: The user wants to update an already existing archive by adding file(s), folder(s), or archive object(s) to it.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The user wants to update an already existing archive by adding file(s), folder(s), or archive object(s) to it.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The user adds file(s) or folder(s) to an already existing archive.
scope_contract.start_boundary: An already existing archive is available to receive additional content, and the user has file(s) or folder(s) to add.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The file(s) or folder(s) are added to the existing archive.
in_scope_actions: Add file(s) to an existing archive
Add folder(s) to an existing archive
Add archive object(s) to an existing archive
excluded_adjacent_actions: Create a new archive by selecting files and folders for archiving
variant_dimensions: type of object added: file(s), folder(s), or archive object(s)

claims.content: User
The target existing archive has already been opened in PeaZip's file manager interface and is the current archive being browsed before the user initiates the Add operation.
The existing archive is in a format that supports modifications; it cannot be a read-only supported format.
One or more objects (files or archives) have been selected by the user to be added to the archive.
With the target existing archive open, the user invokes the Add action by selecting 'Add' from the toolbar or menu, or by pressing Ctrl+A.
Following the User's invocation of the Add action, the selected objects are added to the current archive.
The User presses the Add button on the toolbar.
The system adds the selected objects to the current archive.

Diverges from Step 1 (select objects from the file manager interface): instead of selecting objects from the file manager interface, the user starts from the search dialog context menu and uses the drag-to-archive action to add files to the existing archive.

Diverges from Step 2 (press the Add toolbar button): instead of pressing the Add toolbar button, the user selects one or more objects in the file manager interface, right-clicks (or uses an equivalent input device), and chooses 'Add' from the context submenu.
Diverges from Step 2 (press the Add toolbar button): instead of pressing the Add toolbar button, the user presses Ctrl+F to add a folder to the archive.

Diverges from Step 2 (press the Add toolbar button): instead of pressing the Add toolbar button, the user drags file(s) and/or folder(s) into the file manager interface while browsing the existing archive; provided the archive format allows modifications, the system adds them to the current archive.

missing_aspects: Source page 27 cited in evidence card EC-AF-010 is not present in the provided document set, preventing verification of the 'File > Add' menu path.

claims.content: At Step 3, if an error occurs during an archive operation and PeaLauncher is configured with 'Keep open only if needed (errors, list, test...)', the launcher window may remain open for diagnostic purposes; the user can terminate the add/archive operation using the Cancel button in the archiving interface.
At Step 3, if a selected object in the archive's layout needs to be removed, the user can remove it using Cancel, Ctrl+R, or Ctrl+Backspace.
At Step 3, if the archive's layout view needs to be updated, the user can use the Refresh function (F5 or the refresh icon) to update the archive's layout view.
The selected objects are added to the current archive.
The updated archive contents are displayed as an overview in the file manager interface, and the archive layout reflects the added objects and can be refreshed using F5 or the refresh icon.
The system displays a progress window indicating that the job was successfully completed, along with details such as input size, output size, and time.

missing_aspects: Explicit confirmation message for adding files to an *existing* archive
Update of the file list view within the existing archive interface after addition
Explicit confirmation message for adding files to an existing archive

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 1 has the User select objects after the Trigger (invoking Add) has already occurred. Since the object selection is also stated as a precondition, this restarts the flow before the initiating action rather than continuing from the Trigger. (coverage-preserving removal: not subsumed (The witnesses mention selected objects and adding them to the archive, but do not explicitly state that the User selects one or more objects or that the selection occurs from the file manager interface.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim at index 1 (Step 3 remove selected object) describes a recovery action using Cancel, Ctrl+R, or Ctrl+Backspace, but does not state a clear exit: it does not say whether the flow returns to a main-flow step, terminates/hands off, or ends in an explicit failure/prevention state. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim at index 2 (Step 3 refresh layout) describes using Refresh (F5 or icon) to update the layout view, but does not state a clear exit: it does not say whether the flow returns to a main-flow step, terminates/hands off, or ends in an explicit failure/prevention state. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 1 describes a remove-object recovery action but does not state what happens after removal: return to a main_flow step, terminate/hand off, or a terminal state. The branch therefore lacks a clear documented exit. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 2 describes refreshing the layout view but not the branch outcome after refresh; it does not state return to a main_flow step, termination/handoff, or a terminal state. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 2 repeats the trigger action ('User presses the Add button') after step 1 has already stated that the selected objects are added. This restarts the Add action within the main flow and contradicts the trigger-to-main-flow sequence.

[trigger_preconditions_coverage] Precondition 3 covers selected files or archives but omits folders, while the goal/scope explicitly includes adding folder(s). For the folder variant, the precondition that folders are selected before the Add trigger is not established.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim at index 1 describes removing a selected object using Cancel, Ctrl+R, or Ctrl+Backspace, but it does not state whether the flow returns to a main_flow step, terminates, or ends in an explicit failure/prevention state.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim at index 2 describes refreshing the archive layout view, but it does not state whether the flow returns to a main_flow step, terminates, or ends in an explicit failure/prevention state.

inconsistency_hints: Precondition 0 only guarantees that the archive is selected or opened, while the Trigger explicitly requires the target archive to be open. The disjunctive precondition does not guarantee the open-archive state required before the User can invoke Add.

The Main Flow starts by having the user select objects (step 1) and then press the Add button (step 2), but the Trigger is already the user invoking Add with the target archive open and objects selected per Preconditions. This makes step 1 precede the Trigger and step 2 duplicate it, so the flow restarts rather than continuing from the initiating event.

Exception flow claim 0 only says the launcher window remains open after an archive error. It does not state whether the add operation is rejected/aborted, whether an error state is shown, or how the flow returns, terminates, or hands off, so the branch lacks a clear documented outcome.
